text:
tala: Minor but annoying onboarding snag: our rust sampleapp failed after upgrading batching helper. Embeddings request to rerank-1 returned payloads with different top-level keys between SDKs.

 diego: what do you mean "different keys"? paste example?

tala: node/python request -> response contains "embeddings" array and optional "embedding_dim". Rust Go sampleapps saw "vectors" and "dim" instead. Our retriever parser expects "embeddings" and blew up at runtime.

yu: oof. SDK parity nightmare. Did the API change? or did batching helper mutate the response?

tala: traced it: server returns a canonical shape but node helper's response-normalizer replaced the top-level key with "embeddings" while rust helper left the raw server key of "vectors" intact. Also in some retry fallbacks a compact variant returns 512 dims and the helper writes embedding_dim=512 even though model param said 768.

sam: can you share minimal request + snippet of the different responses? redact floats ok.

tala: request:
```js
client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood/rerank-1', input: ['s1','s2'], batch_size: 2, retry: { max_attempts: 2 } })
```
node-normalized response (trimmed):
```json
{ "model": "redwood/rerank-1", "embeddings": [[0.1,...],[0.2,...]], "embedding_dim": 768 }
```
rust-raw response (trimmed):
```json
{ "model": "redwood/rerank-1", "vectors": [[0.1,...],[0.2,...]], "dim": 768 }
```
When node retried due to a 429 it sometimes switched to rerank-1-small (dim 512) and wrote embedding_dim: 512. Rust helper left dim header in x-redwood-model-variant only.

diego: summary: three gaps: key naming (embeddings vs vectors), dim field name (embedding_dim vs dim), and fallback variant leak (small variant dims).

ryan: cause is likely SDK response normalizers and inconsistent header->body propagation across SDKs. Also the batching helper's fallback default was set in the node config earlier and slipped into sampleapp.

sam: immediate mitigations we should recommend to customers?

diego: 1) normalize at app-level: check for response.embeddings || response.vectors and response.embedding_dim || response.dim. 2) assert vector length: if (vec.length !== expectedDim) log and fail loudly. 3) disable implicit fallback on critical pipelines: retry: { fallback_model: null }.

yu: I'll add a tiny polyfill snippet to the onboarding sampleapps across SDKs to avoid this bite:
```js
const raw = await client.embeddings.create(...)
const vectors = raw.embeddings || raw.vectors || []
const dim = raw.embedding_dim || raw.dim || (vectors[0] && vectors[0].length)
if (!vectors.length) throw new Error('empty embeddings')
if (dim !== expectedDim) throw new Error(`unexpected dim ${dim}`)
```

ci-bot: Created task DEVEX-4357: sdk-parity-embed-keys-and-fallback-dim; assigned @ryan.

ryan: plan for the PRs: 
- harmonize SDK normalizers to expose a single canonical response key: response.embeddings and response.embedding_dim, not rewrites.
- surface x-redwood-model-variant as response.model_variant across SDKs.
- remove implicit fallback default from node batching helper and add explicit config opt-in.
- add sampleapp polyfill and an onboarding checklist item: "assert embedding shape + log model_variant".

sam: also add a short FAQ on docs: "why did my embedding dim change?" and include troubleshooting steps.

tala: confirmed polyfill fixed the crash locally. I'll drop a tiny doc PR running through the error message and recommended config. Thanks :raised_hands:

ryan: marking this high priority for SDK parity. Will ping platform about including model_variant in customer-facing logs too.

sam: nice. once tasks land, we should run a quick smoke across all sampleapps to validate they handle both key names and variances.

tala: agreed. closing the loop here.
